markdown.headingText: Cast Hierarchical List into Dimensional list
markdown.markdown:
### Description cast_hier2dim() casts a hierarchical list into a dimensional list (i.e. into a recursive array).
hier2dim() takes a hierarchical list, and predicts what dimensions the list would have, if re-casted by the cast_hier2dim() function.

### Usage 
cast_hier2dim(x, ...)

hier2dim(x, ...)

## Default S3 method:
cast_hier2dim(x, in2out = TRUE, maxdepth = 16L, recurse_classed = FALSE, ...)

## Default S3 method:
hier2dim(x, in2out = TRUE, maxdepth = 16L, recurse_classed = FALSE, ...)
### Arguments
x a list.
If x has redundant nesting, it is advisable (though not necessary) to reduce the redundant nesting using [dropnests](dropnests.qmd).
... further arguments passed to or from methods.

in2out see [broadcast_casting](aaa02_broadcast_casting.qmd).
maxdepth a single, positive integer, giving the maximum depth to drop nesting in.
The surface-level elements of a list is depth 1, so maxdepth must be >= 2.
recurse_classed TRUE or FALSE, indicating if the function should also recurse through classed lists within x, like data.frames.
### Value For cast_hier2dim():
A recursive array (i.e. a dimensional list).

For hier2dim():
An integer vector, giving the dimensions x would have, if re-casted by cast_hier2dim().

### Examples ```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA} library("broadcast") # ideal scenario ==== x <- list( group1 = list( id1 = list( height = rnorm(10, 170), weight = rnorm(10, 80), sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE) ), id2 = list( height = rnorm(10, 170), weight = rnorm(10, 80), sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE) ), id3 = list( height = rnorm(10, 170), weight = rnorm(10, 80), sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE) ) ), group2 = list( id1 = list( height = rnorm(10, 170), weight = rnorm(10, 80), sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE) ), id2 = list( height = rnorm(10, 170), weight = rnorm(10, 80), sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE) ), id3 = list( height = rnorm(10, 170), weight = rnorm(10, 80), sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE) ) ) ) print(x) hier2dim(x) # predict what dimensions `x` would have if casted as dimensional x2 <- cast_hier2dim(x) # cast as dimensional # since the original list uses the same names for all elements within the same depth, # dimnames can be set easily: dimnames(x2) <- list( names( x[[1]][[1]] ), names( x[[1]] ), names( x ) ) print(x2) # very compact, maybe too compact...? # print a small portion of the list, but less compact: cast_dim2flat(x2[, 1:2, "group1", drop = FALSE]) ```
